fullPassage:
According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. The second is natural happiness, and we experience it when we do get what we want. In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness. Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value. Choosing synthetic happiness produces comparable positive outcomes, health advantages, and a similar sense of well-being.
For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you.
Surround yourself with people who inspire you and embrace you. Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely admire, those who bring positivity into your life, and, most importantly, those who make your day brighter.
Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. When you appreciate what's already in your life, you begin to value these things more. In return, they bring you more happiness. Without valuing what you already have, it's challenging to express thankfulness for anything else.
Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy and satisfied. As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that enhance your overall happiness levels.

questions.passage:
According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types.

(A) Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.
(B) The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. The second is natural happiness.
(C) In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 두 유형 소개(B) → 사회적 편견(C) → Nevertheless 반박(A).
det.analysis: ✅ (B)-(C)-(A): 정의 → 편견 → 반박의 논리적 흐름. Nevertheless가 (C)의 편견을 반박. ❌ 나머지: 논리 흐름 깨짐.
det.tip: Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고): 앞 내용을 반박. (C) 뒤에 와야 자연스러움.

questions.passage:
Try to smile, even if you don't really want to.

(A) As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that enhance your overall happiness levels.
(B) A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it.
(C) Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy and satisfied.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미소의 힘(B) → 뇌 신호(C) → 결과(A).
det.analysis: ✅ (B)-(C)-(A): 일반적 효과 → 구체적 메커니즘 → 'As a result' 결과. ❌ 나머지: As a result는 마지막이어야 함.
det.tip: As a result(결과적으로): 앞 내용의 결과. 마지막에 와야 자연스러움.

questions.passage: Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. ① When you appreciate what's already in your life, you begin to value these things more. ② In return, they bring you more happiness. ③ Without valuing what you already have, it's challenging to express thankfulness for anything else. ④
questions.stem:
다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"In short, gratitude is the foundation of true happiness."

det.korean: '요컨대, 감사가 진정한 행복의 기초'는 전체 내용을 요약하는 결론.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: 문단의 마지막에 요약 문장. 'In short(요컨대)'는 결론 연결어. ❌ ①②③: 중간에 요약은 어색.
det.tip: In short(요컨대): 글의 요약/결론. 문단 마지막에 위치.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. ① The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. ② The second is natural happiness, and we experience it when we do get what we want. ③ In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness. ④ Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.
questions.stem:
다음 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"However, Dr. Gilbert's research challenges this common assumption."

det.korean: '그러나 길버트 박사의 연구는 이 보편적 가정에 도전한다'는 편견(③) 뒤, 반박(④) 앞.
det.analysis: ✅ ④: (③)의 편견을 'this common assumption'으로 받고, Nevertheless로 이어지는 구조. ❌ ①②: 아직 편견 언급 전. ❌ ③: 두 유형 정의 사이.
det.tip: 'this common assumption' = natural happiness is superior. However로 전환 후 Nevertheless로 근거 제시.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be ①<u>divided</u> into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness. In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is ②<u>superior</u> to synthetic happiness. Nevertheless, synthetic happiness holds equal significance. Choosing synthetic happiness ③<u>produce</u> comparable positive outcomes. The power to ④<u>choose</u> happiness lies within you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 인위적 행복을 선택하는 것이 만들어낸다. Choosing(동명사 주어) = 단수.
det.analysis: ✅ ①divided: can be divided. ✅ ②superior: be superior to. ❌ ③produce: Choosing(동명사 주어, 단수) → produces. ✅ ④choose: to choose(to부정사).
det.tip: 동명사 주어 = 단수 취급: Choosing produces (O) / Choosing produce (X).

questions.passage: Surround yourself with people who ①<u>inspire</u> you and embrace you. Healthy and meaningful friendships are ②<u>built</u> on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely admire, those who bring positivity into your life, and, most importantly, those ③<u>who</u> make your day brighter. Focus on what you have, not on what you don't ④<u>having</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 가지고 있지 않은 것에 집중하지 마라. don't have.
det.analysis: ✅ ①inspire: people who inspire(관계대명사절). ✅ ②built: are built on(수동태). ✅ ③who: those who(관계대명사). ❌ ④having: don't + 동사원형 have. having은 문법 오류.
det.tip: 조동사 don't + 동사원형: don't have (O) / don't having (X).

questions.passage: For every minute you ①<u>spend</u> feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. When you appreciate ②<u>what</u>'s already in your life, you begin to value these things more. Without ③<u>valuing</u> what you already have, it's challenging to express thankfulness. A smile has the power ④<u>boosting</u> your mood and bring happiness to those who see it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 미소는 기분을 좋게 하는 힘이 있다. power to V(to부정사).
det.analysis: ✅ ①spend: spend + time + V-ing. ✅ ②what: 관계대명사 what. ✅ ③valuing: Without + 동명사. ❌ ④boosting: the power to boost. power 뒤 to부정사.
det.tip: the power to V: ~하는 힘. the power boosting (X) → the power to boost (O).

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness, and it happens when we feel happy even when we don't get what we want. In our society, we hold the belief that natural happiness is ①<u>superior</u> to synthetic happiness. Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal ②<u>significance</u> and lasting ③<u>value</u>. Choosing synthetic happiness produces comparable positive outcomes, health advantages, and a ④<u>different</u> sense of well-being.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 인위적 행복은 비슷한(similar) 안녕감을 만든다. different(다른)는 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①superior: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②significance: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③value: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④different: 원문은 similar. 동등하다는 맥락에서 '다른'은 모순.
det.tip: similar(비슷한) ↔ different(다른). comparable = similar.

questions.passage: Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to ①<u>boost</u> your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends ②<u>signals</u> to the brain that there is cause to be happy and ③<u>satisfied</u>. As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that ④<u>weaken</u> your overall happiness levels.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 뇌가 '기분 좋은' 화학물질을 방출하여 행복 수준을 향상(enhance)시킨다. weaken(약화)은 부적절.
det.analysis: ✅ ①boost: 원문 그대로. ✅ ②signals: 원문 그대로. ✅ ③satisfied: 원문 그대로. ❌ ④weaken: 원문은 enhance. 행복을 약화가 아닌 강화.
det.tip: enhance(향상시키다) ↔ weaken(약화시키다). feel-good chemicals = 행복 강화.

questions.passage: For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you. Surround yourself with people who inspire you and embrace you. Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. Try to smile, even if you don't really want to.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

The passage mainly suggests that happiness is a matter of personal __________.

det.korean: 글의 핵심: 행복은 개인의 선택의 문제.
det.analysis: ✅ ②choice: 'The power to choose happiness lies within you' 일치. ❌ ①wealth(부): 무관. ❌ ③talent(재능): 무관. ❌ ④luck(운): 반대.
det.tip: choose happiness: 행복을 선택하다. 글 전체가 선택적 행동 강조.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Dr. Gilbert's view challenges the common belief that __________.
ch: only getting what we want can make us truly happy
happiness cannot be divided into categories
synthetic happiness is more valuable than natural happiness
all forms of happiness are equally short-lived

det.korean: 길버트의 관점은 원하는 것을 얻어야만 진정으로 행복하다는 편견에 도전.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 자연적 행복 우월 = 원하는 것 얻어야 행복. 이것이 편견이라는 주장. ❌ ②: 분류 불가는 주장 아님. ❌ ③: 인위적이 더 가치 있다 아님. ❌ ④: 모두 단명이라 아님.
det.tip: natural happiness is superior = only getting what we want makes us happy. 이 편견을 반박.

questions.passage: Surround yourself with people who inspire you and embrace you. Healthy and meaningful friendships are built on mutual support for each other's happiness. Choose friends whom you genuinely admire, those who bring positivity into your life, and, most importantly, those who make your day brighter.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 영감을 주고 포용하는 사람들과 함께하라고 권한다
건강한 우정은 상호 지지 위에 세워진다
친구 선택에서 가장 중요한 것은 학업 성적이다
삶에 긍정을 가져다주는 친구를 선택하라고 한다

det.korean: 가장 중요한 것은 하루를 밝게 하는 사람. 학업 성적 언급 없음.
det.analysis: ✅ ①②④: 원문 일치. ❌ ③: 'most importantly, those who make your day brighter'. 학업 성적 아님.
det.tip: most importantly: 가장 중요하게. 하루를 밝게 하는 사람이 핵심.

questions.passage: Focus on what you have, not on what you don't have. When you appreciate what's already in your life, you begin to value these things more. In return, they bring you more happiness. Without valuing what you already have, it's challenging to express thankfulness for anything else.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 이미 가진 것에 감사하면 더 큰 행복을 얻는다
가진 것의 가치를 모르면 새로운 것을 더 잘 감사한다
행복은 가지지 못한 것을 추구할 때 온다

det.korean: 이미 가진 것에 감사하면 더 큰 행복을 얻는다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: 'appreciate → value → bring you more happiness'. ❌ ②: 없는 것 집중은 반대. ❌ ③: 가치 모르면 감사 어려움. ❌ ④: 반대.
det.tip: Focus on what you have: 가진 것에 집중. 없는 것이 아닌 있는 것.

questions.passage: For every minute you spend feeling unhappy, frustrated, anxious, or stressed, you lose a precious moment of happiness. The power to choose happiness lies within you. Surround yourself with people who inspire you. Focus on what you have. Try to smile. Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 'The power to choose happiness lies within you'가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 행복은 외부 환경이 아닌 자신의 내면에서 결정된다

det.korean: '행복을 선택하는 힘은 당신 안에 있다' = 행복은 자신의 내면에서 결정.
det.analysis: ✅ ②: 'lies within you(당신 안에 있다)' = 내면에서 결정. ❌ ①: 타인이 아닌 자신. ❌ ③: 전문가 불필요. ❌ ④: 선택(choice)이 필요.
det.tip: lie within: ~안에 있다. 행복의 원천은 외부가 아닌 내면.

questions.passage: Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy and satisfied. As a result, your brain releases "feel-good" chemicals that enhance your overall happiness levels. <u>This</u> shows that even a simple action can have a powerful effect on our emotions.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'This'가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the fact that smiling triggers feel-good chemicals
the importance of choosing good friends

det.korean: 미소가 기분 좋은 화학물질을 촉발한다는 사실이 간단한 행동의 효과를 보여준다.
det.analysis: ✅ ③: This = 앞 문장 전체(미소 → 뇌 신호 → 화학물질 방출). ❌ ①②④: 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: This = 앞 내용 전체. 미소의 메커니즘과 결과.

det.korean: 원하는 것을 얻었을 때 = natural happiness.
det.analysis: ✅ natural: 'we experience it when we do get what we want'.
det.tip: natural happiness = 자연적 행복. 원하는 것을 얻으면 느끼는 행복.

questions.passage: Try to smile, even if you don't really want to. A smile has the power to boost your mood and bring happiness to those who see it. Even a small smile sends signals to the brain that there is cause to be happy and satisfied.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

The customer expressed her __________ (satisfy) with the excellent service.

det.korean: 고객은 서비스에 대한 만족을 표현했다.
det.analysis: ✅ satisfaction: her + __________ → 명사. satisfy(동사) → satisfaction(명사).
det.tip: satisfy(만족시키다, 동사) → satisfaction(만족, 명사). -faction 접미사.

questions.passage: According to Harvard psychologist Dr. Daniel Gilbert, happiness can be divided into two types. The first is called synthetic happiness. In our society, __________. Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ the belief / is / that / to / we / natural happiness / hold / superior / synthetic happiness ]

accept: we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness
We hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness
we hold the belief that natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness.

det.analysis: ✅ we hold(동사) + the belief(목적어) + that(동격접속사) + natural happiness is superior to synthetic happiness(동격절).
det.tip: hold the belief that: ~라는 믿음을 가지다. superior to: ~보다 우월한.

det.analysis: ✅ A smile has(주어+동사) + the power to boost(to부정사) + and bring(병렬) + to those who see it(관계대명사절).
det.tip: the power to V: ~하는 힘. those who: ~하는 사람들.

"그럼에도 불구하고, 실제로 인위적 행복은 동등한 중요성과 지속적 가치를 가진다."

Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.

det.korean: Nevertheless, in practice, synthetic happiness holds equal significance and lasting value.
det.analysis: ✅ Nevertheless(그럼에도 불구하고) + in practice(실제로) + holds(가지다) + equal significance(동등한 중요성) + and lasting value(지속적 가치).
det.tip: Nevertheless: 그럼에도 불구하고. in practice: 실제로. hold: 가지다.
